candidates.source_body_excerpt: Residents in a busy Middleton street want councillors to rethink parking restriction plans outside their homes. On Thursday, Middleton Township Committee will consider objections to proposed parking restrictions in Grimshaw Lane where there have been issues with speeding, serious crashes, including a fatality, as well as inconsiderate parking causing issues for buses. In a report to the committee, Rochdale Council Highways said: “The north-western section of Grimshaw Lane, between its junctions with Greengate and Townley Street, has historically been reported by bus operators as a key location with poor service punctuality and reliability. “The council considers that congestion, particularly during peak and school activity periods; a prevalence of informal parking with frequent vehicle movements delaying the passage of through traffic; and obstructive parking (including near bus stops, around side road junctions and at pedestrian crossing locations) impacts operational safety along this particular route section. “The proposal includes intended provision of new footway build-outs to reduce the width of side road pedestrian crossing widths at Sedgley Street, Sandy Lane, and (Old) Sandy Lane junctions with Grimshaw Lane. “Furthermore, it is proposed that three new pedestrian refuge islands are also installed to assist crossing at key locations, with two refuges along Grimshaw Lane (east and west of its junction with (Old) Sandy Lane) and across Sandy Lane. “Supporting installation of these new refuge islands, it has been necessary to promote parking protection by way of new localised sections of double-yellow line(s) sufficient to accommodate the safe unobstructed passage of all vehicles including allowance for refuse collection and for HGVs associated with the numerous industrial premises along the subject corridor.” The proposals include extending bus stop bays at several locations; adding double yellow lines along much of the northern side of Grimshaw Lane, particularly from Saxon Street to Sedgley Street, and to introduce marked bays for resident parking.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: An innovative Rochdale company is a real high flier in aerospace and defence. From precision engineering to next-generation aerospace technology, NEMA is helping put Rochdale on the global advanced manufacturing map. It was established in in 1954 as The Nordale Spring Company to supply the aerospace industry with components. In 2003, it changed its name to Nordale Electro-Mechanical Actuation (NEMA). For almost 70 years, NEMA has been designing and manufacturing precision-engineered motors, generators and components from its Rochdale base and has been supported on its journey by Rochdale Development Agency. Today, based at Chichester Business Centre, the company is recognised as one of the UK’s leading specialists in high-performance aerospace components, machinery and systems, supplying customers across the global aerospace and defence sectors. From concept development and prototyping through to qualification, production and aftermarket support, NEMA provides customers with complete engineering solutions that help bring advanced aerospace technologies into service with confidence. Then Mayor of Rochdale Cllr Janet Emsley speaks to NEMA staff. Image: Rochdale Council The business has developed expertise in electrification technologies that support the aviation sector’s transition towards more-electric and hybrid-electric aircraft, helping customers improve efficiency, reduce weight, increase reliability and lower environmental impact.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Toothless Walsall played out a fourth goalless draw in eight games as lowly Rochdale grafted for a hard-earned League Two point. Walsall steadily built pressure after a tame opening, Nils Ramming producing a smart double stop at the near post from Mason Hancock and Aaron Pressley after 25 minutes. Dale grew into the game, with Dajaune Brown's cushioned effort from the left edge of the area hitting the face of the bar in the 29th minute, while the Derby loanee's low drive was pushed around the near post one-handed by Jed Ward five minutes before half-time. Hancock had a close-range shot saved, with James Connolly's follow-up header scrambled off the line by Dan Moss seven minutes into the second half, and, while the Saddlers maintained pressure, the final ball was lacking. The home side's fortunes were summed up when Harvey Gilmour's kamikaze backpass went straight to Pressley, only for the striker to gift Kaiden Wilson a chance to clear with a heavy touch 11 minutes from time. Substitute Lewis Simper's bicycle kick flew straight into Ramming's gloves deep into added time, but there would be no breakthrough. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Lee Grant says Walsall need to find a way to translate draws into wins, after his side were forced to settle for a point in their goalless stalemate against Rochdale at Bescot. Walsall extended their unbeaten league start with a third successive draw, but have failed to find the net in each of their last two games, after drawing 0-0 at Exeter City in the previous weekend. Aaron Pressley came close for Walsall in the first half and James Connolly had a header cleared off the line, but Walsall were ultimately unable to find a way through. And Grant admitted that his team need to rediscover that killer instinct in order to get back to winning ways. “In all three of those games, you can argue that you should win, but we never take anything away from the opposition,” head coach Grant said. “For Crewe to score in the 90th whatever minute, I think you’ll hear me after the game saying well played Crewe and well done for sticking at it. “Even though I would’ve liked for us to get that one over the line. And today, I’ll say well done Rochdale and well done on your organisation and work ethic, even though we should win the game. “So we’ve got to find a way in the games we should win, to win. In the games where we have to be resolute, and fight and scrap, then fine. “We know there’s a really high benchmark now for the group on that stuff. We don’t take it for granted, we don’t rest on our laurels with it and the clean sheets are evidence of it. “But we know that we’ve got growth in other areas as well.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale boss Ian Watson hailed the “warriors” who fought for a precious point in a 0-0 draw at Walsall days after he received a vote of confidence. Dale released a statement in support of the summer appointment on Wednesday following one win from five League Two matches since promotion from the National League under Jimmy McNulty. While Walsall had 70 per cent possession and 24 shots, Watson’s men kept clear opportunities to a minimum, hit the bar through Baba Adeeko after half-an-hour and carried the greater threat late in the first half. Watson said: “Sometimes you need to set up a little bit differently away from home and we talked about Walsall being in a really good moment. “We spoke about the mentality we would need, being warriors and stopping the ball going in our net, making sure we were all connected and working hard without the ball. “We didn’t want as many moments without the ball as we had, we caused way too many turnovers and that allowed them to come on to us, but you could see how much the players wanted to run and get in the way. “They were really willing to work hard for the supporters and the club, we saw that really connected group that wanted to do everything it possibly could not to lose.” Walsall pressure built after a tame start, with Nils Ramming producing a smart double stop at the near post from Mason Hancock and Aaron Pressley after 25 minutes.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale boss Ian Watson hailed the “warriors” who fought for a precious point in a 0-0 draw at Walsall days after he received a vote of confidence. Dale released a statement in support of the summer appointment on Wednesday following one win from five League Two matches since promotion from the National League under Jimmy McNulty. While Walsall had 70 per cent possession and 24 shots, Watson’s men kept clear opportunities to a minimum, hit the bar through Baba Adeeko after half-an-hour and carried the greater threat late in the first half. Watson said: “Sometimes you need to set up a little bit differently away from home and we talked about Walsall being in a really good moment. “We spoke about the mentality we would need, being warriors and stopping the ball going in our net, making sure we were all connected and working hard without the ball. “We didn’t want as many moments without the ball as we had, we caused way too many turnovers and that allowed them to come on to us, but you could see how much the players wanted to run and get in the way. “They were really willing to work hard for the supporters and the club, we saw that really connected group that wanted to do everything it possibly could not to lose.” Walsall pressure built after a tame start, with Nils Ramming producing a smart double stop at the near post from Mason Hancock and Aaron Pressley after 25 minutes. Adeeko’s cushioned effort from the left edge of the box hit the face of the bar after 29 minutes and Dajaune Brown’s low drive towards the near post drew a smart save from Jed Ward five minutes beforehalf-time. Walsall skipper James Connolly’s follow-up header was scrambled off the line by Dan Moss seven minutes into the second half and, while the Saddlers kept plugging away, the killer ball was lacking. Harvey Gilmour’s kamikaze backpass went straight to Pressley 11 minutes from time, but a heavy touch allowed Kaiden Wilson to clear and Walsall’s fourth 0-0 draw in eight games was confirmed when Lewis Simper’s bicyclekick flew straight into Ramming’s gloves deep into added time, leaving boss Lee Grant with a “weird” mix of emotions. “It is probably as proud as I have ever been as a head coach or manager,” he said. “To put together a new group, 15 new faces, and for a really good team to come here and give us that amount of respect shows us where we are. “At the same I am bitterly disappointed that we dropped two more points at home in a game that we have to win. Our deficiencies are clear, the group has owned them, I own them and I take full responsibility along with theplayers. “While we can be really proud of what we’re giving, the control and the dominance, it doesn’t mean a great deal if we don’t put it to bed.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Lee Grant says he was left with mixed emotions after Walsall were unable to find a way past Rochdale in their goalless stalemate at Bescot. Walsall had 24 shots and dominated possession, but were forced to settle for a third successive draw on a frustrating afternoon. Aaron Pressley saw his close-finish blocked behind in the first half, while James Connolly had a header scrambled off the line shortly after the restart. Rochdale also had chances, as Bada Adeeko hit the crossbar and Dajaune Brown forced a smart save from Jed Ward in close proximity to one another in the first period. “There are probably two emotions. It’s probably the most proud I’ve been as a head coach ever,” head coach Grant said. “To put a group of players together. 15 new faces being in each other’s company for a very short space of time and then for a really good team to come here and give us that sort of respect. “And to fight and work against us the way they did, shows us where we’re at and what the group has earned with their performances and with their work to this point. “So incredibly proud of that and at the same time bitterly disappointed that we dropped two more points here at home in a game that we have to win.” He continued: “Our deficiencies currently are clear, but the group have owned them, as do I and take full responsibility for that. “Whilst we can be really proud of what we’re doing. The control, the dominance, 24 shots and 70 per cent possession, it doesn’t really mean a great deal if we don’t put that to bed. “Two feelings both present in me at the moment. So a weird feeling.”

The event is being organised by Rochdale Borough Council with the local veterans’ community.

The evening will recognise the service and sacrifice of past and present Armed Forces personnel.

It will include music from military bands, an act of remembrance and historic war stories.

Guests are expected to include the Mayor of Rochdale, MPs, councillors and representatives from the Armed Forces.

Any money raised will go to the Mayor of Rochdale’s charities for 2026 and 2027.

They are Rochdale Veterans Breakfast Club, Rochdale Women’s Welfare Association, SANDS, Springhill Hospice and The Christie.

Mayor of Rochdale Councillor Faisal Rana said: “This will be a special evening as the Armed Forces community unites to pay its respect to the brave women and men for their service and sacrifice. It is sure to be a moving and memorable night in the stunning setting of the Great Hall at Rochdale Town Hall.

“We last held a Festival of Remembrance in 2019, so this will be a poignant occasion as we bring together the Armed Forces family under one roof. As a veteran, I understand the importance of recognising the service and sacrifice of our Armed Forces, as well as the council’s ongoing support for our military personnel.”

Tickets cost £15 and include a pie and pea supper.

They can be purchased through the Your Trust Rochdale website.

One of the main reasons being that the cost of a licence for each show has reached way over £1,500. We feel sad for the children who thoroughly enjoyed being connected with the production and the confidence that they found. Due to this decision we still have many boxes of unsold costumes and it looks as if we will not be using them again. Middleton Labour said three people had been staying in tents at the cemetery, including two people described by the group as white British.

In an update published on social media, the councillors said police attended the site following a multi-agency meeting.

They said one man was arrested for immigration offences and detained by police before being referred to Immigration Enforcement.

The group said the other two people had been offered temporary accommodation but declined it.

Rochdale Council's rough sleepers outreach team had been working with the people for several weeks and would continue to offer support, according to the post.

Middleton Labour said all three people had now moved from the cemetery.

The council's Environmental Management Team was also sent to the site to remove rubbish, litter, fly-tipping, damaged bins and abandoned tents. Strimming work had also started.

The councillors said all three tents had been slashed overnight after posts circulated on social media describing the site as a "migrant camp".

They said police were looking for the person responsible and appealed for anyone with information to contact Greater Manchester Police on 101.

Middleton Labour also said police were monitoring social media after comments threatening violence were posted online.

People who experience hate crime or racial abuse were urged to report it to police.

Crimes can be reported to Greater Manchester Police on 101 or online, with 999 used in an emergency.

Rochdale Council's Community Safety Team can be contacted on 0300 303 8878 and its homelessness team on 0300 303 8875.

Around £15 million will be spent on cost of living support for Rochdale borough residents over the next three years.

The package, approved by councillors at a recent cabinet meeting, will use money from the government’s Crisis and Resilience Fund.

The funding will provide support for residents in Heywood, Middleton, Pennines and Rochdale who are facing financial hardship.

Help will include emergency payments, support with heating costs, debt and welfare advice, housing support, food and other essential goods and access to free warm spaces.

The Crisis and Resilience Fund replaces the Household Support Fund and provides councils with three years of government funding for locally delivered crisis support.

Money will also be invested in welfare advice, debt support, employment opportunities and other services intended to help residents increase their income and manage household costs.

The Holiday Activities Fund programme will continue to provide healthy meals, activities and free childcare places for hundreds of young families during school holidays.

Councillor Neil Emmott, leader of Rochdale Borough Council, said: “Throughout my time as council leader I have ensured we have a helping in place for those residents in Heywood, Middleton, Pennines and Rochdale who are most in need. I am proud of our work to support low-income families across the borough and this builds and enhances the assistance we have put in place over recent years.

“I am delighted to be working in partnership with the government, helping to alleviate people’s cost of living caused by many factors out of our control. Along with the government’s welcome decision to remove the two-child benefit cap and expand free school meals, this cash injection will ease pressures on household budgets and help to tackle the long-term causes of poverty. My message is clear, if you are facing a financial crisis, please get in touch with the council we are here to help.”

Further information is available at www.rochdale.gov.uk/costofliving.

The council’s cost of living helpline is available on 01706 923685 from 9am to 5pm, Monday to Friday.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: An off-licence plan which triggered concerns about underage drinking and anti-social behaviour will be decided next week. Rochdale Council’s Licensing Sub-Committee will resume its decision over plans to sell alcohol at the RJ Store, which is being created at 190 Rochdale Road, Middleton. In March, RJ Group MCR Ltd applied to the council for an off-premises licence for the former Middleton Cars and Black Bull Fencing site. Greater Manchester Police and Rochdale Trading Standards raised concerns and several public objections were lodged against the application including fears it would increase in underage drinking and anti-social behaviour in the residential area. The licensing committee considered the application in May but adjourned its decision because it wanted the applicant to be present to address the issues raised. In a report to the latest panel, a licensing officer notes that Greater Manchester Police raised concerns that the original 7am to midnight licensing hours were “excessive” and “could potentially lead to anti-social behaviour during the late-night hours”. It added that “the applicant has since agreed with GMP and Trading Standards to accept the licensing conditions around CCTV and the protection of children from harm and also to amend the proposed application hours to the supply of alcohol” from 7am to 11pm.
